newsitem.title: USA: Albright to visit Denver on summit plans.
newsitem.headline: Albright to visit Denver on summit plans.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will visit her American hometown of Denver next week to discuss plans for holding the June 20-22 "summit of eight," grouping major industrialised nations and Russia, the State Department said on Thursday.

Some members of the Denver community were reportedly concerned that the summit will take place at the same time as the trial of Oklahoma bombing suspect Timothy McVeigh but department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the city could cope with both high-security events.

"Secretary Albright intends to travel to Denver next Tuesday, where she'll meet with the mayor, other community leaders, organisers of the G-8, the Group of Eight summit in Denver, and also make a public appearance and talk to some of the citizens of Denver," Burns said.

He said that Denver was where she lived and went to school after emigrating to the United States to escape communism after the Second World War and where her father was a professor at the University of Denver.

"So she's looking forward to going back. She does want to just take stock of how the preparations are proceeding for the Denver summit. It's a very, very important summit" in which Russia will play an elevated role, he said.
Albright will "discuss specifically any way that we can further the preparations for Denver," he said.

Burns said that when the decision was made last year to locate the summit of the eight in Denver, it was not known that the McVeigh trial would also be held there. McVeigh is charged with the April 19, 1995, bombing of the Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City that killed 168 people.

"So we have to live with the McVeigh trial. It's a very important trial for the American people," Burns said, adding: "The summit ... and the trial can go on simultaneously and effectively and productively. And we don't believe the trial is going to upset in any way the planning for the summit or the implementation."
